## Natural history notes

A large longtail skipper characterized by brown wings, pale translucent spots on the forewings, and long tail-like extensions on the hindwings. In Florida, it is common in gardens, fields, roadsides, forest edges, parks, agricultural areas, and other sunny habitats where legumes and nectar plants are available. Adults feed on nectar from many flowers, while the caterpillars feed on plants in the pea family, especially beans and related vines, often tying or folding leaves together to form protective shelters.
